set.title: The modular AI stack by Netresearch
set.description: Netresearch’s ten open-source modules for AI in TYPO3: role, maturity, requirements, dependencies and limits, and which ones run in this lab.
set.abstract: Ten modules from Netresearch for AI in TYPO3, with their limits and owners.

set.header: A modular AI stack for TYPO3
set.subheadline: Introduce AI in TYPO3. Keep control of models, costs and access.

set.header: AI in TYPO3: problems, questions and requirements
set.subheadline: A talk by Sebastian Mendel, Netresearch DTT GmbH, at MTUG – TYPO3 User Group München on 9 November 2026. The texts below come from Netresearch’s stack page, in Netresearch’s own English; the “In this lab” column is ours.

set.title: Modular AI stack
set.description: Netresearch’s overview of the ten modules, with current releases and requirements.

set.content:
Connect language models centrally, support your editors and add the functions you need. Ten open-source components can be combined to suit your use case. The independent browser assistant answers questions about the current page.

Work with your existing TYPO3. The server-side AI foundation supports TYPO3 13.4 and 14.3. nr-repurpose requires TYPO3 14.3 and PHP 8.3.

Start with a small scope. nr-llm with nr-vault for a shared provider connection. Passkeys and a backend agent are additional choices.

Check maturity per module. From stable tools to alpha: status, release and evidence are listed in the comparison.

set.header: Which task do you want to address?

set.title: Protect access, secrets and HTTP destinations
set.content:
Credential management, optional passkeys and controlled outbound HTTP requests.

nr-vault manages API keys with envelope encryption. Passkeys add passwordless sign-in. nr-http-guard checks outbound HTTP destinations on the registered TYPO3 RequestFactory path and bound guard clients.

Separate sign-in, permissions and HTTP protection Passkeys authenticate people; TYPO3 permissions define their access. Passkeys are optional for the AI foundation, but nr-passkeys-fe requires nr-passkeys-be. HTTP Guard does not automatically protect Vault: its optional adapter integration is needed. Independent SDK/Guzzle clients and direct cURL/socket calls are outside the protected path.

set.title: Connect language models centrally
set.content:
Manage providers, models, budgets and server-side usage.

nr-llm connects consuming extensions to configured language models. nr-mcp-agent adds a backend assistant and is at alpha maturity.

The server-side path nr-llm requires nr-vault. The backend agent is optional. Built-in writing tools require approval. TYPO3 administrators set the approval requirement for remote MCP tools per server.

set.title: Create editorial content
set.content:
Write in the editor, repurpose sources and prepare landing pages.

cowriter assists writing in CKEditor. nr-repurpose turns existing sources into further formats. nr-landingpage guides the creation of a landing page.

Check requirements before selecting nr-repurpose requires TYPO3 14.3 and PHP 8.3. Models must support the functions you need. Review drafts and sources before publication.

set.title: Add channel publication
set.content:
A separate integration to plan and verify.

No ready-made social publishing integration verified against the current stack is offered here.

This integration boundary is open Older examples such as rx-scheduled-social, t3socials and pb_social are not recommendations for TYPO3 13.4/14.3. Importing a feed does not provide outbound publication.

set.header: Browser AI is an independent path
set.content: nr-browser-ai answers questions about the current page directly on suitable devices running Chrome. It requires neither nr-llm, vault nor passkeys and has no central usage logs or budgets. An initial model download is needed; other visitors see the configured fallback.

set.content:
• The modules support technical controls. That does not establish blanket conformity with the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF or ISO/IEC 42001.
  • A shared interface does not guarantee equal model capabilities or equivalent answers. Switching provider requires suitable functions and a use-case evaluation.
  • Vault protects credentials. Business knowledge sources, search indexes, data permissions and source quality must be configured separately.
  • This page provides no evidence of savings, faultless answers or a production-ready social publishing integration.

set.title: Do I need all ten modules?
set.content: No. nr-llm requires nr-vault. The backend agent and content tools are additional, individually selectable consumers of nr-llm. Passkeys and HTTP Guard are separate choices; nr-passkeys-fe requires nr-passkeys-be. HTTP Guard requires neither Vault nor passkeys. nr-browser-ai works independently. The table lists direct Netresearch dependencies and version requirements.

set.title: Does HTTP Guard automatically protect all outbound connections?
set.content: No. After activation, nr-http-guard covers the registered TYPO3 RequestFactory path and clients created by its guard factories. Configured policies, exceptions and enforce, observe or disabled modes still apply. Vault needs the optional adapter integration; independent SDK/Guzzle clients, early bootstrap requests and direct cURL/socket calls need their own integration. The published version is alpha for evaluation.

set.title: Where are API keys stored?
set.content: The local default adapter of nr-vault stores encrypted secret values and encrypted data keys in the database. The master key lives outside it. Consuming extensions use vault identifiers. The goal is to avoid plaintext keys, not database storage itself.

set.title: Do budgets and logs cover every use of AI?
set.content: User budgets and usage recording are available for server-side calls routed through nr-llm. The budget check uses recorded usage and any known cost estimate. Requests already in progress can exceed the limit. This accounting covers integrated calls only. nr-browser-ai runs locally in the browser and deliberately has no central usage history.

set.title: Can sensitive data stay inside our environment?
set.content: Suitable self-hosted models can support that. Review the complete data flow, including fallback configuration, tools and knowledge sources. OpenAI compatibility describes an interface, not a processing location.

set.title: What about social network publication?
set.content: It remains a separate integration project. Based on published package requirements, the earlier rx-scheduled-social, t3socials and pb_social examples are not recommendations for TYPO3 13.4/14.3. Verify maintenance, current channel APIs and approvals before choosing a solution.
